featured_reviews.review_text: As a student in the Psychology Department at Bhavan’s College, I’ve found the environment to be really positive and motivating. featured_reviews.review_text:
Bhavan's College was the institute where I spent my college career spanning 5 years. I can write a novel about this place but I'll keep it short and sweet.
The college undoubtedly has undoubtedly the biggest campus among any in Mumbai. There's a temple, a huge playground, a volleyball court, a plant nursery, a pond and a great amount of lush green trees all around the campus. There are many faculties for students to choose from too. I graduated from here in 2005 but whenever I'm in Mumbai I always visit Bhavan's college to refresh my memories and relive the golden years of my youth.
During the monsoon season, the campus is green and gives you a very satisfying vibe. There are many cafeterias around and inside the campus making it one of the most happening colleges in Mumbai. I understand that a lot changes over time but the memories associated with your friends and professors never fade away with time.

featured_reviews.name: Pratyush Mohite
featured_reviews.review_text:
Every student has a different perspective about college. What may seem bad to one student might be perfectly fine for another. However, as a recent 12th pass-out who studied at Tolani College during both 11th and 12th grade, I can confidently say that my experience was excellent.

If you are genuinely interested in studies and willing to learn, Tolani College is one of the best places you can choose. The quality of teaching is impressive and, in my opinion, often better than many coaching classes that charge several times more than the college fees.

One of the biggest strengths of this college is its teachers. I was fortunate to learn from supportive and dedicated teachers such as Sangeeta Ma'am and especially Melba Ma'am, who guided me tremendously in Mathematics. Their patience, teaching methods, and willingness to help students made a huge difference in my academic journey.

The college has experienced teachers for different subjects, each bringing their own teaching style and positive attitude to the classroom. Beyond academics, the college also organizes meaningful competitions and activities that help students develop confidence, skills, and memorable experiences.

My advice to future students is simple: attend lectures regularly, interact with your teachers, and don't hesitate to ask questions whenever you have doubts. The faculty is genuinely supportive and willing to help students who show interest in learning.

As for some of the negative reviews online, I believe many of them come from students who rarely attended lectures or had issues due to their own behavior and expectations. While everyone is entitled to their opinion, my personal experience was overwhelmingly positive

Our experience with Tolani College of Commerce (Junior College) has been extremely disappointing. While the administration appeared supportive during admissions, the reality afterwards has been unprofessional and deeply unsatisfactory. Class teacher Ms. Melba have been dismissive of both parents and students. Despite providing medical documentation, my child’s health issues were repeatedly labelled as “excuses”.
teachers engaged in name-calling and bullying, even though the college had formally accepted medical grounds for attendance. Instead of support, there has been constant badgering by nearly all teachers about attendance, creating unnecessary mental stress.
No genuine academic or emotional support has been provided to the student. On the contrary, staff have used hand gestures ridiculing both parents and children, which is insulting and unprofessional.
As a parent, I too faced disrespect. Ms. Melba raised her voice and even demanded an apology from me when I raised valid concerns.
•	Administrative functioning is equally poor and chaotic — exam schedules and timetables are circulated irregularly and at the last minute, leaving families stressed and unprepared.

Such repeated patterns of bullying, ridicule, and poor communication highlight what feels like a substandard institution in terms of professionalism and values. Families expect empathy, dignity, and consistent support from educators — unfortunately, that has not been our experience at Tolani College of Commerce (Junior College).

Don’t ever send your child here

featured_reviews.name: Ritu Kothari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Before you pay ₹6-10 Lakhs to IIDE, read this once. Honestly, I held back from writing this for a while, but I think people deserve to know before they spend this kind of money.

The fees are ₹6L for PGDM and ₹10L for UG. I thought it would be worth it. It wasn't. Their own external faculty told us in class that the same content is available outside for ₹50K to ₹1L. I still think about that.

The quality of teaching was disappointing. A few teachers were genuinely good but most were not at the level you'd expect for this price. After I joined a marketing company my seniors were shocked at the gaps in my knowledge. That moment told me everything. Also teachers here teach topics halfway and you don't even realize what's missing until real work exposes it.

Placement is where it really fell apart for me. You get 5 chances, but they find every reason to use them up fast, counting intro calls and jobs you found yourself. If you found a job on your own through LinkedIn or Naukri and told them about it, they'd say, "Oh, we have connections there; let us help." They never help, but they counted that as one of your chances. They do nothing to help and still count it as one of your chances. Once your 5 are gone, they're done with you.

And if someone from IIDE referred you here, just know they get paid ₹30K to ₹50K for that referral. Keep that in mind when reading their glowing reviews.

Please do proper research before joining. Talk to students who are not referring you. Ask for full batch placement data in writing. I really wish I had done that.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually never write negative reviews, but after studying in this college and seeing the experience of so many students around me, I genuinely feel people deserve to know the reality before taking admission here.

The college presents itself very differently during admissions compared to what students actually experience later. During counseling, students are promised quality education, practical exposure, workshops, photography, makeup, styling classes, industry learning, and many other opportunities. But once admissions are done, most of these things either never happen properly or are reduced to very short sessions that barely teach anything meaningful.

One thing that shocked many students was the lack of transparency in fees. Students in the same batch and same classroom were paying completely different amounts for the exact same course. It honestly felt unfair and unprofessional.

Another major issue is the environment students have to deal with after joining. Instead of feeling supported, many students constantly feel stressed, pressured, and unheard. Whenever students try to raise concerns or complaints, they often feel discouraged from speaking openly.

What disappointed me the most was how the college handled reviews. Students were literally called one by one from classrooms and asked to write positive reviews in front of staff members. Many times, students were guided on what to write instead of being allowed to honestly share their real experiences. Because of this, I personally feel many online reviews do not reflect the actual reality students face after admission.

This college may look attractive during the admission process, but please research properly, talk to genuine students privately, and think carefully before investing your time, money, and future here. Education should feel supportive and inspiring, not mentally exhausting.

featured_reviews.name: Dawné DWN
featured_reviews.review_text:
This college is one of the biggest scams disguised as an educational institution. If you genuinely care about your future, mental peace, money, and education, stay as far away from this place as possible.

The admission process is nothing but manipulation and marketing. During counseling, Diana ma’am will make endless promises and sell you dreams about exposure, professional training, opportunities, practical learning, workshops, fashion industry preparation, photography, makeup, styling, and so much more. They know exactly how to emotionally convince students and parents into taking admission. But the moment your fees are paid, the entire reality changes.

One of the most disgusting things about this college is the complete lack of transparency in fees. Students sitting in the SAME classroom, studying the SAME course, in the SAME batch, are charged completely different amounts. It literally feels like bargaining in a market instead of a professional educational institution. Some students are overcharged heavily while others pay much less for the exact same education.

And what education are they even providing? Most of the things they promise are never taught properly. Classes like photography, makeup, and other “specialized subjects” are reduced to random one-hour sessions just so they can claim they covered it. There is no depth, no proper guidance, no serious teaching, and no real effort to prepare students for the industry. Half the students are left teaching themselves everything.

The environment after admission becomes mentally exhausting. Mamta ma’am and Sunita ma’am create so much pressure and stress that students genuinely start regretting joining this college. Instead of helping students grow, the administration makes students feel trapped, unheard, and constantly anxious.

And the worst part? Whenever students try to question management, complain, or speak up about genuine issues, fear tactics start. Students are made to feel like their exams, marks, or even degrees could be affected if they create “problems.” Many students stay silent simply because they are scared of consequences.

This college does not just waste your money — it destroys confidence, motivation, mental health, emotional health, and even physical health from the amount of stress it creates. The amount of disappointment students experience here is unreal.

Please do not fall for the fake promises during admission. There are far better colleges out there that actually care about students and education. Even if another college costs slightly more, at least you will get professionalism, support, proper faculty, and an environment where students are respected instead of emotionally drained.
